text:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing a federated hotpath for inference. goal is to decouple session orchestration from the token-generation runtime so we can tranche tech debt and roll pieces independently. feedback?

maya: +1 on the intent. can you sketch ownership boundaries?

alex: rough idea: session-controller (state, auth, routing) -> owns prefix cache reference and routing decisions. inference-core -> owns kv cache implementation, batching, quantized kernels. interface = thin request/response with KV hints.

juan: worried about cross-tenant cache invalidation. how do we surface cache sharding without coupling routing?

alex: plan: shard by tenant-id at session-controller level, pass shard-id in header X-Cache-Shard. inference-core treats it opaque. avoids per-tenant logic in runtime.

nora: that helps but what about failover semantics? if runtime falls back to CPU quantized variant, we need consistent prefix semantics.

alex: agree. propose a compatibility contract: cache keys must be stable across model variants. doc link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/hotpath-federation (WIP)

maya: can we add a small adapter that normalizes keys pre-insert so older variants still hit? keeps runtime simple.

juan: rollout strategy? we should tranche debt: 1) split session-controller interface, 2) deploy inference-core side-by-side, 3) canary routing, 4) full cutover.

alex: exactly. suggested canary window 72h and traffic ramping 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 days.

nora: add automatic rollback on latency p95 regression >30% or increased error-rate >1%. we should also measure token-cost delta.

maya: ops question: what infra changes? need separate autoscaling for inference-core, and maybe a small sidecar for cache coordination during migration.

alex: infra: new k8s deployment per inference-core variant, metrics exported: per-variant latency, batch-size, token-rate. sidecar optional but recommended for staged migrations.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: alex/hotpath-federation-spike -> staging. status: queued. :rocket:

juan: long-term debt-tranching note: keep the session-controller small — avoid folding batching logic back in. otherwise we reintroduce coupling.

alex: agreed. next steps: i'll update RFC with ownership matrix, error contract, and rollout playbook. @maya can you draft the autoscaling SLOs?

maya: on it. will share a PR by EOD. :+1:

nora: I'll add rollback hooks to the runbook and make sure oncall knows the thresholds.

alex: thanks all. will post the RFC PR link here when ready.
